text:
Alex: Hey team — quick Q. I'm planning to relocate to Ireland in June while on parental leave. Want to confirm: 1) Will my Redwood health benefits continue? 2) Can IT ship my company laptop to Ireland or should I return it before I go? 3) Any payroll/tax or immigration paperwork I should know about? cc @Jess @Marta @Leo

Sam (People Ops): Congrats — exciting! Short answers up front: benefits maybe; device shipping possible but needs export/compliance signoff; payroll/tax depends on tax residency and local rules. Can you share exact travel dates and whether this is temporary (<=90 days) or longer? Also please fill the International Leave Request form: https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/international-leave

Alex: Thanks — plan is 2026-06-10 to 2026-08-10 (~61 days). Will stay with partner's family, temporary address is: 3 Clonmel Rd, Dublin. I want to keep Redwood medical if possible and avoid returning the laptop if shipping is allowed.

Jess (Benefits): Thanks for the dates, Alex. For a ~61-day stay the US medical plan can usually continue, but we need: 1) a temporary address, 2) confirmation of dates, and 3) a signed acknowledgment that local care may not be covered abroad. Please attach a passport copy + temporary address proof to the benefits case. Deadline: submit docs by 2026-05-20 to avoid coverage gap. If you end up exceeding 90 days we'll need to transition you to local coverage.

Marta (Payroll): Heads up on payroll/tax: short temporary stays (<183 days) generally keep US payroll, but cross-border tax treaties vary. For ~61 days we typically keep US withholding, however you must complete the International Payroll Checklist and the 'Temporary Foreign Address' payroll form: https://intranet.redwood/payroll/intl-checklist.pdf. If you receive any local income while abroad (unlikely) notify payroll immediately. Please submit checklist by 2026-05-20 so we can confirm withholding.

Leo (IT): Re: laptop — we prefer you return company devices to US inventory for any multi-month move, but shipping to EMEA is doable with export compliance. Two options: 1) Ship device to Ireland (company pays shipping and temporary import paperwork). We need an Export Compliance Form and an approval from Security before shipping. Expect 7-10 business days processing. 2) Return laptop to office before you leave and we'll issue a loaner (EU partner laptop) via remote checkout for the duration. That avoids export paperwork. If you want option 1 open a ticket to #it-ops with subject: "Intl Ship Request — Alex" and include passport + travel dates.

Alex: Leaning toward option 2 to keep it simple unless benefits require device in-country for work. I'll coordinate with Nora to return laptop and request a loaner.

Tara (Manager): I approve the loaner plan. Oncall coverage: Alex — please add the 3-week handoff doc and mark yourself as \"limited availability\" in PagerDuty for the leave window. Nora agreed to cover Weeks 1-3 for critical pages; Sam — can you confirm we need any formal oncall handoff paperwork in People Ops?

Sam (People Ops): For parental leave we normally require a 1-page handoff and a manager sign-off. I'll drop a checklist here: - Handoff doc (owner, critical runbooks, emergency contact) - Oncall reassignment in PagerDuty + calendar blocks - Return-to-work check-in scheduled 2 weeks before end date I'll email the template to you, Alex, and ping Nora.

Alex: Updated — handoff doc in Google Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/parental-handoffs/alex-dublin-2026. I've added calendar blocks and set PD to limited availability. I'll submit International Leave and Payroll forms by EOD Friday.

hr-bot: People Ops received a new International Leave submission from Alex. Ticket #PO-3742. Please attach proof of temporary address and passport scan within 5 business days to avoid delays.

Jess (Benefits): Noted — once we have the address + passport we'll confirm medical continuity and share an acknowledgment form to sign. If anything changes (dates extend) flag us ASAP.

Marta (Payroll): Thanks — once checklist is in we'll confirm withholding status. If any statutory reporting is required for EMEA payroll we will loop legal.

Leo (IT): I'll standby on the #it-ops ticket. If you go with the loaner, please drop off the current device to HQ IT by 2026-06-03 so we have time to prepare the EU loaner.

Tara (Manager): Thanks all. Alex — ping me if you want me to approve any last-minute exceptions. Happy to help with the forms. :thumbsup:

Alex: Really appreciate everyone — I'll submit forms today and follow up here.

Sam (People Ops): Great — marking this thread as tracking: International leave (temporary relocation) + parental leave coverage. I'll follow up with checklist email and confirm once payroll/benefits/it signoffs are complete.
